thread:
Maya: heads up — deploy (release/3.14.0) pushed canary a few mins ago, seeing a ton of alerts from the latency SLO. :rotating_light:
Maya: not sure if it's real user impact yet, canary traffic 10% but p50/p95 have spiked
IncidentBot: Pager triggered for channel eng-oncall — SLO burn detected for service `text-gen-proxy` (>15min). Escalation: Maya, Sam.
Maya: @Sam you around? I'm on the rollout but can grab the kill-switch if you can check dashboards
Sam: on it, joining now. what's the canary id?
Maya: canary id `canary-2026-03-15-03` — DeployBot logs showing repeated 503s to /v1/generate, but infra health checks are green
DeployBot: Deployment canary-2026-03-15-03: 10% traffic routed. Observed 503 spikes at 2026-03-15T03:07Z, error rate 7% (expected <0.5%).
Jordan: I can look at routing and LB — might be affinity or a bad instance. pulling pod logs now.
Eli: I'm with prod infra, spinning up a probe to isolate host-level latency.
Maya: quick sanity check: customer-facing app errors? we have a couple complaints in #support, but not widespread yet.
Sophie: support says a handful of enterprise customers saw 500s for generation requests — seems correlated to the new model variant.
Sam: can anyone open the canary dashboard? the usual dashboard is empty for this release (didn't get created by the CI), I'm getting a blank graph.
Jordan: confirmed — dashboard `canary/3.14.0/latency` missing. alerts are firing off generic SLO-rule that references that dashboard tag, which is why it's noisy.
Maya: ugh — so alerts are real but less context. I'm going to flip the feature flag for the new model variant to kill traffic to the canary. prepping the flag toggle now.
Sam: I'll take pager while you flip. taking over oncall :hand:
Sam: toggling flag `ff:model-3-14-canary` -> `off` :

```
# featureflagctl
featureflagctl set ff:model-3-14-canary false --env=prod --actor=maya
```

Sam: flag flip confirmed by DeployBot. routing should start to fall back to canary-0 (stable) within 30s.
DeployBot: Feature flag update applied. Traffic rebalanced. Canary traffic now 0%.
Eli: I'm still seeing elevated p95 on a subset of hosts — looks like some sticky KV cache entries from the canary variant that didn't get cleared. running cache flush on affected nodes.
Jordan: rolling restart of the 3 nodes that served the canary; `kubectl rollout restart deployment/text-gen-proxy -n prod --selector=canary=true`
Maya: support updated customers and queued a blitz of manual retries to clear their jobs.
Sophie: customers report improvements after retries, one enterprise still reporting intermittent latency.
Sam: SLO burn stopped trending up after the flag flip but we still have alerts queued because the alerting rule aggregates on the missing dashboard metric (which is being backfilled slowly).
Maya: ok — mitigation steps so far: 1) feature flag kill -> removed canary traffic, 2) restarted affected nodes, 3) cache flush, 4) customer retries via support.
Jordan: root cause hypothesis: the new model variant introduced a slightly different tokenization layer that caused increased memory churn + occasional 503s under the canary traffic profile. It also didn't register metrics under the canonical dashboard tag due to a config change in the model server. hence missing dashboard and confusing alerts.
Eli: can reproduce locally with a scaled-down load profile, will send reproducer script.
Sam: quick remediation checklist for now: make the canary dashboard optional creation in CI, add a guard in alerting so a missing dashboard/tag doesn't trigger noisy paging, and ensure feature flag canary rollback is tested.
Maya: agreed. I'm going to hand off final monitoring steps to Jordan — I'm going to start a formal incident page so we can capture timeline.
Jordan: taking it — I'll create a minimal temp dashboard to provide context and suppress duplicate alert noise. linking it here: https://console.redwood.ai/dash/temp/1938456789
IncidentBot: Incident created: INC-2026-03-15-47 — Severity: P2. Assigned: Jordan.
Sam: leaving pager to Jordan, I'm back to normal rotation. :thumbsup:
Maya: quick note for postmortem: missing dashboard + metric tag regression caused escalation noise and delayed diagnosis. feature flag kill worked but we should ensure rollback path includes automated cache reset for model servers.
Sophie: I'll coordinate with support to surface impacted customer list for the postmortem and outreach.
Jordan: action items I'm adding now: [1] Add dashboard creation check to release CI (owner: Jordan) [2] Add alerting guard: if metric tag missing, don't page production SLO — page a diagnostics channel instead (owner: Eli) [3] Add automatic cache-clear hook on rollback/flag flip (owner: Maya) [4] Run simulated canary with tokenization memory profile (owner: Sam). ETA for tasks: one week for the CI/dashboard fixes, shorter for the alert tweak.
Eli: uploading reproducer gist and logs to the incident doc.
Maya: thanks all. closing this thread once the temp dashboard is stable and alerts are quiet.
Jordan: created incident doc and linked follow-ups in the ticket. will post a short blameless postmortem in #postmortems tomorrow with timeline and customer impact summary. :spiral_notepad:
IncidentBot: Incident INC-2026-03-15-47 status updated -> Monitoring.
Maya: :heart: great coordination, appreciate the fast kill and handoff.
Sam: nice work team.
Sophie: adding customer outreach draft to the doc now.
Jordan: last note — mitigate noisy alerts immediately after deploys by adding a 5min silence window for SLO alerts on canary releases until dashboards are populated. I'll propose the exact silence window in the follow-up.
